title: Screen blanking after a configurable idle delay
description:
Why: a static screen (especially the status line) can burn in on some monitors.

Scope:
- New append-only setting: Blank after off / 1 / 5 / 10 / 30 / 60 min (values to decide).
- Idle = no key pressed and (decide) no serial output / no screen change; the machine and terminal keep running while blanked.
- Blank by having core 1 output black lines (keep DVI sync, so the monitor does not go through a resync on wake); no change to the screen buffer. A video.c flag latched per frame like the other per-frame state.
- Wake on any key; the waking key is swallowed (DEC behaviour) - confirm. Wake on host output optionally.
- SET-UP open = not idle. Host tests for the idle timer logic in a portable module.

title: Setting to hide the status line

Why: the status line is not always wanted (and is the main burn-in risk).

title: Firmware update from SET-UP (no reboot into CP/M mode)
description:

Scope:
- A SET-UP key (e.g. U, shown only when FIRMWARE.UF2 is present, like monitor.c firmware_offered()) in both modes.
- Terminal mode does not touch the SD card today: mount it on demand (sdcard + FatFs) when the key is pressed, not at boot.
- Reuse uf2.c/fwupdate.c (check -> stage with progress -> rename to FIRMWARE.OLD -> unmount -> commit); share the confirm/progress text with the monitor rather than duplicating it. setup_feed runs inside the USB stack, so defer the work to the main loop as drivepanel does.

- If USB mass storage lands (qur.3), accept FIRMWARE.UF2 from the USB drive too.

Acceptance: update from terminal mode on hardware; test coverage for the SET-UP key path where portable.

title: Settings lost on reflash: UF2 E10 block erases the last flash sector
description: The SDK adds an RP2350-E10 workaround block (family absolute, 0x10ffff00) as the first UF2 block. On the 4 MB flash it wraps to 0x103fff00, so every drag-and-drop flash erases the last sector: settings slot 1. When the newest record was in slot 1, the older slot 0 record (e.g. the previous Mode) came back.
design: Settings sectors moved one sector down (size - 3 sectors); old slot 0 becomes new slot 1, so existing records carry over. Fixed uncommitted; needs a hardware check: save Mode twice (both slots), reflash, Mode kept.
close_reason: Verified on hardware

title: Z80 host-file port device and CP/M IMPORT/EXPORT tools for a FAT folder
description:
Why: lets CP/M programs copy files between CP/M disks and plain FAT files, the core of the file-transfer work (see the planning ticket, which may reshape this).

Sketch (to confirm in planning):

title: Plan: moving files into and out of the CP/M machine without pulling the SD card
description:
Why: all machine data lives in .DSK images on the one SD card, so getting a file in or out today means power off, pull the card and use image tools (cpmtools etc.) on a PC. Planning ticket: decide the design, then file/adjust the implementation tickets under qur.

Questions to settle:
- Media: (a) a folder on the existing SD card (fz80-style IMPORT/EXPORT folders; still needs a card pull to reach the PC, so only half a fix), (b) USB mass storage on the host port next to the keyboard (best long term; hot-pluggable, no machine shutdown), (c) a second SD slot on SPI1 (free pins GP8-11). Recommendation to evaluate: build the Z80-side interface against FatFs paths so the media is just a volume (0: SD, 1: USB), do (a) first, then (b).
- Z80 interface: a new port device (machine.c, like port 8) with a command/status/data protocol (fz80-firmware/firmware/fZ80.7/SDz.h has SVC_IMPORT/EXPORT/IMLIST/EXLIST as a reference) vs. mapping a FAT directory as a CP/M drive (much harder: CP/M directory emulation).
- CP/M tools: e.g. IMPORT.COM / EXPORT.COM / a DIR-like lister, written in Z80 asm like worms.asm, assembled at build time and put on CPM22 by diskimg_gen.py --file.
- 8.3 name mapping (no LFN in ffconf), user areas, text vs binary (^Z padding to 128-byte records, trimming on export), wildcards, overwrite rules.
- Coexistence with drives.c keeping images open on the same volume, and the 250 ms write flush.
- SRAM budget (~28 KB free): FatFs FIL objects, buffers; TinyUSB MSC host class cost.
- Alternatives worth one line each in the decision: XMODEM over SIO2/UART0, or the host tools/hostbridge.py path.

title: Escape parser stuck in an unterminated OSC/DCS string: end strings on CR/LF (xterm brokenStringTerm) plus a length limit
description:
Why: the escape parser can get stuck discarding a string forever, and then the screen stops updating. ESC ] (OSC) and ESC P / ESC X / ESC ^ / ESC _ (DCS, SOS, PM, APC) put vtparse in OSC_STRING (src/vtparse.c:198) or STRING (src/vtparse.c:203). It leaves only on ESC, CAN or SUB, plus BEL for OSC. There is no length limit and no timeout, and the 8-bit ST (0x9C) is ignored because c1_controls is off (src/vtparse.c:92). After that, every printable byte is thrown away.

It is easy to trigger by accident. Alt-modified keys send a bare ESC prefix (src/keyboard.c:233-235), so Alt+], Alt+Shift+P, Alt+Shift+X, Alt+Shift+6 (^) and Alt+Shift+- (_) each open a string. So does any CP/M program that echoes an ESC-prefixed key it read, or a host that sends a truncated sequence. F11 (dmt.34) and SET-UP R (dmt.35) now get you out of it, but nothing stops it from happening.

What, after xterm's brokenStringTerm resource. XTerm Control Sequences (patch #411) describes it as "exit string mode if it decodes a common control character such as carriage return before the string terminator"; it is xterm's workaround for programs that leave strings unterminated:

1. In OSC_STRING and STRING, a C0 control other than BEL (in OSC) ends the string and goes back to GROUND. At least CR and LF should do this; most likely every C0 except BEL should. The control is then executed as usual, so the CR or LF still takes effect. This terminal discards the contents of every string anyway, and none of the strings it is likely to receive contain C0 controls (window titles, OSC 52 base64, DECRQSS, sixel), so nothing is lost. With this rule, pressing Return after an accidental Alt+] fixes things straight away.
2. As a backstop, limit the length of a discarded string (a counter in vtparse_t; for example 512 or 1024 bytes, which is about GNU screen's 768). At the limit, go back to GROUND; the rest of the string then prints as text. Other programs use limits like this (screen 768, xterm.js 10 MB, Emacs xterm-max-cut-length "to protect users from runaway sequences"). Keep it well above the longest string a host is likely to send to this terminal.
3. Optional, separate decision: accept 8-bit ST (0x9C) as a string terminator even when c1_controls is off. It is never a UTF-8 lead byte, but it can be a UTF-8 continuation byte, so it could end a string early. Leaving this out is fine.

Out of scope: Alt sending an ESC prefix is standard (xterm metaSendsEscape) and stays as it is.

Tests (test/test_vtparse.c and test/test_term.c):
- ESC ] text CR, then more text: the later text prints and the CR takes effect.
- ESC P with no terminator, then LF: the parser is back in GROUND.
- OSC still ends on BEL and on ESC \; existing test_ignored_sequences still passes.
- A string longer than the limit goes back to GROUND at the limit; vtparse_reset() and each new string clear the counter.
- Sixel-like DCS data with no C0 controls is still discarded completely up to ESC \.
- README Limitations or terminal section: note the behaviour.

title: F11 in CP/M mode should reset the terminal, not just the Z80 machine
description:
Why (reported by the user): "a reset through F11 does not reset the colors/terminal state when it should". In CP/M mode F11 goes reset_key() (src/main.c:449) -> cpm_reset() (src/main.c:640), which flushes the drives, drops the typed-ahead key queue and calls machine_reset() - but never touches term_t. So leftover SGR / DECSCNM / DECCOLM / origin mode / scrolling region survive a reset, and a program that left fg == bg stays unreadable. F11 is expected to act like the reset button of a real machine, which would also reset the terminal.

The freeze this was seen with: cpm_reset() prints "*** Reset" and reboots the Z80, and the rebooted program sends its init sequences (worms.asm SINIT = ESC [ 0 m ESC [ ? 25 l ESC [ 2 J), so a full reboot normally clears the colours. It does not when the escape parser is wedged - see dmt.33.

What: in cpm_reset() (src/main.c:640), call term_reset() after machine_reset() and before term_puts("\r\n*** Reset\r\n"), so the banner and the rebooted program start from a known state. Needs dmt.33 for the term_reset() API.

Terminal mode is deliberately out of scope: F11 there is a function key sent to the host as ESC [ 2 3 ~ (src/keyboard.c:76, src/keyboard.c:205-206) and the escape hatch for that mode is the SET-UP R reboot - tracked separately.
notes: Implemented: cpm_reset() calls term_reset() before the drive-A check (so the monitor path is reset too) and, per the user, switches back to the SET-UP width (default_columns, the last applied Columns setting, set in apply_settings) via term_set_columns when it differs; the status line redraws through screen_resets. README F11 and Columns rows updated. Awaiting hardware check: in CP/M, leave colours/DECSCNM/132 cols/wedged ESC ] then F11.
close_reason: Verified on hardware

title: Add term_reset(): a public terminal reset that also clears the escape parser
description:
Why: after a freeze the terminal has no local reset at all. reset() is static in src/term.c:214 and there is no API to force one, so nothing can clear leftover SGR colours, DECSCNM, DECCOLM, origin mode or a scrolling region from outside. RIS (ESC c, src/term.c:550) also does not reset the vtparse state, so a host reset cannot recover a wedged parser.

What:
1. Add void term_reset(term_t *t) to src/term.h. Implement in term.c by exposing the existing static reset(), then calling sync_cursor() so screen->cursor_col/row are refreshed.
2. Route RIS (esc_dispatch case 'c', src/term.c:550) through term_reset().
3. reset() should clear t->last_char: after a reset REP (CSI b, src/term.c:464) can currently repeat the character printed just before it.

Related (not in this issue): term_reset() is what lets a user recover from a wedged parser, but it does not prevent the wedge. vtparse can sit in STRING (src/vtparse.c:198) or OSC_STRING (src/vtparse.c:193) forever - entered by ESC P / ESC X / ESC ^ / ESC _ / ESC ] - with no length bound and no timeout, and 8-bit ST (0x9C) is ignored because c1_controls is off (src/vtparse.c:86). Alt-modified keys emit a bare ESC prefix (src/keyboard.c:233-237), so Alt+], Alt+Shift+P, Alt+Shift+X, Alt+Shift+6 and Alt+Ctrl+/ all trigger it, as does any CP/M program that echoes an ESC-prefixed key it read. See the VT510 RM ch.4 behaviour ("ignores all following characters until it receives a SUB, ST, or any other C1 control character") and note xterm et al. rely on a length bound - Emacs ships xterm-max-cut-length for exactly this. Tracked separately.

Tests (test/test_term.c): term_reset restores default fg/bg after SGR 30;40m plus reverse, clears DECSCNM, resets margins and origin mode, homes the cursor, shows the cursor, and recovers the screen after a wedged ESC ].
notes: Implemented: vtparse_reset() (back to GROUND, keeps callback/c1_controls, safe from the callback); public term_reset() = vtparse_reset + reset + sync_cursor; RIS goes through it; reset() clears last_char. Width deliberately not touched by term_reset/RIS (host ESC c keeps width, as xterm). Tests: test_term_reset, test_term_reset_recovers_wedged_parser (OSC, DCS, mid-CSI), test_reset_forgets_rep_char, vtparse test_reset. Awaiting hardware check together with dmt.34.
close_reason: Verified on hardware

title: Palette-indexed cell colours: xterm-256 palette table on core 1, swappable without rewriting the screen
description:
Switching the Palette setting between colour and mono only affects text written afterwards; changing Colors recolours by value (screen_recolour), also hitting ANSI colours equal to a default. Cause: term.c resolves SGR colours to final RGB222 at write time and screen cells store only that.

Design (agreed 2026-10-02, replaces dmt.30):
- Cells (screen_line_t fg/bg, raster_line_t fg/bg) hold an 8-bit xterm-256 palette index; no reserved entries. SGR 39/default fg -> 7, bold default fg -> 15, SGR 49/default bg -> 0. Bold brightens ANSI 0-7 -> 8-15 at write time; reverse swaps indices; 38;5;n stored exactly; 24-bit and RGB -> nearest xterm cube/grey entry. Nothing written depends on the palette.
- Core 1: colour_words grows to 256 RGB565 words (pixel doubled); raster_compose indexes it directly. Two tables, pointer latched at frame start (no half-swapped frame). Palette change = new table, no re-render, no screen_recolour.
- src/palette.[ch] (portable) builds the table from settings (Colors x Palette):
  - White + Colour: 0-15 our ANSI set, 16-255 standard xterm (cube 0/95/135/175/215/255, greys 8+10n).
  - Phosphor (green/amber/blue) + Colour: 0-15 a ramp in the phosphor hue, 16-255 xterm colour.
  - Any + Mono: all 256 entries as a ramp in the hue (white -> grey).
  - Ramp for 0-15 by bands: 0 = 0; 8 ~35%; 4,1,5,2,6,3 ~45-60%; 7 = 67% (today's fg); 12,9,13,10,14,11 ~75-92%; 15 = 100% (today's bold fg). Mono 16-255: luminance mapped into 35-100% (0 only for black).
- main.c picks indices for the status line, SET-UP panel and drive letters per settings (white: 15 on 4; phosphor/mono: 0 on 7) and redraws them in apply_settings as today. term_set_colours, screen_recolour, term_mono_colours, the mono path in term.c go away. Settings record unchanged.
- SET-UP palette preview shows the edited palette live (restore on cancel). Splash keeps its own 4 colours (tint from the hue).
Known trade-offs: default fg == SGR 37 and default bg == SGR 40; similar-luminance colours look alike in mono; phosphor + colour shows ANSI as phosphor but 256/24-bit colours in colour.
acceptance_criteria:
- Switching Colour <-> Mono and changing Colors recolours everything on screen immediately, both directions, without rewriting cells
- 38;5;n shows the exact xterm colour (RGB565); 24-bit maps to the nearest entry
- Status line, SET-UP panel, CP/M console and splash still correct in all 8 Colors x Palette combinations
- Host tests: palette tables, term indices (SGR, bold, reverse, 256/24-bit), raster compose via table; scripts/test.sh and firmware build pass; video_stats().late not worse on hardware
notes: Implemented on branch palette-index (uncommitted): src/palette.[ch] + test_palette; term.c writes indices (TERM_DEFAULT_COLOUR now 0x100, attr fg/bg uint16_t); screen_recolour, term_set_colours/palette, term_mono_colours removed; raster_compose takes a 256-word table; video_set_palette double-buffers, core 1 latches at frame start; settings_colours -> status indices + logo_fg; SET-UP shows the edited palette live (main.c show_palette in setup_service, restored on cancel); demo shows xterm 16-255 swatches. Host tests and firmware build pass; __end__ 0x20077f4c -> 0x200790d8 (+4.4 KB; palette_build is 2.2 KB of code). Phosphor hues (palette.c hues[]): green 33ff33, amber ffb000, blue 3399ff. Awaiting hardware check: 8 Colors x Palette combos, live preview + cancel, 256-colour test (e.g. a 256-colour chart script), status line, logo tint, video_stats late.

title: Z80 core traps DD/FD prefixes before opcodes that do not use HL (EXZ80DOC stops at DD 40)
description: EXZ80DOC stopped in 'ld <bcdexya>,<bcdexya>' with 'Unknown instruction DD 40'. A real Z80 ignores a DD/FD prefix before an opcode that does not use H, L or (HL) (4 T-states, then the opcode), but z80pack's simz80-dd.c/-fd.c map 170 such entries to trap_dd/trap_fd (OPTRAP2). ALT_Z80 handles prefixes properly but ran EXZ80DOC ~25% slower (109 s vs 87 s on the host).
design: Fixed in the vendored core (lib/z80pack, UPSTREAM.md lists it): trap_dd/trap_fd back PC up to the opcode and return 4. OPTRAP stop reasons show the opcode bytes. test_cpu (CPU_TESTS=1) runs EXZ80DOC: all tests successful on the host. Needs hardware check.

title: Monitor N (new disk): no progress, slow for 8 MB
description: Creating an 8 MB disk takes a long time and nothing on screen says it is working; when it ends the screen shows the menu heading ('Z80 CP/M machine (z80pack Z80 core)'). Cause: drives_create runs in the main loop and blocks it, so video_update never runs and the 'Writing NAME.DSK...' line is only drawn at the end, together with the menu. It writes 512 bytes per f_write and sdcard.c writes one block per CMD24, so ~16k single-block writes for 8 MB.
design: 1) monitor_platform_t gets a flush hook (main: video_update) and drives_create a progress callback (every ~256 KB: a dot or percentage, then flush). 2) Write in bigger chunks (e.g. the monitor's 16 KB install window passed in) so FatFs hands disk_write several sectors, and implement multi-block writes in sdcard.c (CMD25, data token 0xFC, stop token 0xFD, wait busy). Same flush/progress for I (install). Host test: the progress callback fires and the image is complete.
notes: Fixed (uncommitted): monitor flush hook (main: video_update), progress dots per 256 KB for N and I, drives_create writes 16 KB chunks, sdcard.c CMD25 multi-block writes. Host tests pass. Needs hardware check: N 8 MB timing, card still reads back OK.

title: HSTX renderer backend (replace PicoDVI/libdvi)
description: libdvi has no HSTX backend (PIO + SIO TMDS encoders only). Write an HSTX driver behind the same cells+scanline renderer interface (GPIO 12-19 only). Start from pico-examples hstx/dvi_out_hstx_encoder.
design:
GOAL: drive DVI from the RP2350 HSTX (hardware TMDS encoder) instead of PicoDVI's PIO serialisers + software TMDS encode; drop lib/PicoDVI.

KEY RISK: 800x600p60 is 40 MHz pixel clock = 400 Mbps per lane. HSTX shifts 2 bits per clk_hstx (DDR), so clk_hstx = 200 MHz (clk_sys 400 MHz / 2). The datasheet rates clk_hstx to 150 MHz (the pico-examples 640x480 demo runs 125 MHz). 640x480 is not an option (132 cols x 6 px = 792 px). Fallbacks if 200 MHz is unstable: 800x600@56 (36 MHz px, 180 MHz), CVT-RB 800x600 (~35.5 MHz, ~178 MHz). Task .1 settles this on hardware before anything else.

HSTX SETUP (from pico-examples dvi_out_hstx_encoder, adapted): bit[2]/[3] = clock (CLK, INV), lanes 0/1/2 -> bits 0/6/4 with SEL_P/SEL_N = lane*10, lane*10+1, odd bit inverted; CSR CLKDIV 5, N_SHIFTS 5, SHIFT 2, EXPAND_EN. Sync/blanking as HSTX_CMD_RAW_REPEAT control symbols, active pixels as HSTX_CMD_TMDS; command lists + DMA ping-pong (2 chained channels, IRQ on core 1). VESA 800x600p60 timing: H 800/40/128/88, V 600/1/4/23, +hsync +vsync (own table; libdvi's goes away).

PIXEL FORMAT: 16 bpp, EXPAND_TMDS lanes R5/G6/B5 (RGB565), RGB222 levels replicated into the bits (2-bit level 0-3 -> 5-bit 0b00000/01010/10101/11111, 6-bit for green likewise) so full scale is ~0xF8, close to today's levels; 2 px per FIFO word, 1.6 KB per line buffer, 80 MB/s DMA. (8 bpp RGB222 with NBITS 2 would cap brightness at 0xC0.) Confirm levels against the PicoDVI build side by side in .1.

RENDERER (core 1, per scanline, into a ring of ~4 line buffers ahead of DMA): budget 1056 px x 10 = 10560 clk_sys cycles/line at 400 MHz; composing 100-132 cells from a 1bpp ink row + per-cell fg/bg is a few thousand cycles. Cursor = swap fg/bg of the cursor cell on blink-on frames; reverse/blink/bold/underline/connectors stay in raster.c.

RASTER FORMAT (raster.c, portable, host-tested): per line slot, stored rows (font rows + 2 padding) of a 1bpp ink bitmap (800 px = 100 B) + per-cell fg/bg (RGB222 after reverse/attrs). Drops the 2-levels-per-8px-group encoder limit: 132-col colours always exact, and 132 cols no longer has to start on an 8-px boundary (can be centred: 4 px). Memory: ~25 x (18 x 100 + 264) = ~52 KB vs 139 KB raster[] today. The 64-px encoder width, 832-px RASTER_WIDTH and TMDS slack all go.

SPLASH: keep the RLE logo data; copy it to SRAM (core 1 must not touch flash; LOGO_IN_FLASH data copied at splash start into the raster memory), core 1 decodes a row of runs per scanline straight into pixels via a 4-entry tinted palette (replaces splash_row_t, splash_map, splash_colour; splash_tint becomes per-level colours). The 2-levels-per-group limit in logo_gen.py can then be relaxed (follow-up).

MIGRATION: .1 is a standalone test-pattern executable (hstx_test) so the main firmware keeps working; .2-.4 switch the firmware over together (raster format change breaks the libdvi path; no dual-backend period); .5 removes PicoDVI and updates docs. Same video.h API throughout.

title: Share one scratch buffer between the monitor (LZ window, blank disks) and the firmware update
description:

Make the buffer generic: a small module (e.g. src/scratch.[ch], portable) that owns one static buffer and hands it out through an interface (acquire with a size, release; or a borrow returning pointer+size), with a check that only one user holds it at a time. The monitor's install/new-disk code and fwupdate's check/stage/commit take their memory from it (fwupdate gets it through the monitor platform hooks or by acquiring it itself). The commit must still read nothing from flash: the buffer stays in .bss, and scripts/check_fwupdate.py must still pass.

title: Flow control as a SET-UP setting: none, RTS/CTS, XON/XOFF
description:
Replace the SERIAL_FLOW_CONTROL build option with a SET-UP setting (saved in flash, applied at runtime like baud/framing from dmt.6) with three choices:

- None (default): GP2/GP3 stay free.
- RTS/CTS: today's hardware flow control on GP3 (RTS out) / GP2 (CTS in), GPIO_FUNC_UART; the RX ring stops draining the FIFO when nearly full so RTS drops. Careful: an unwired CTS can hold TX forever (see VIDEO_DIAG note in main.c); switching pins at runtime must restore them to plain GPIO when leaving RTS/CTS.
- XON/XOFF: receive side sends XOFF (DC3, 0x13) when the RX ring passes a high-water mark and XON (DC1, 0x11) when it drains below a low one (queued ahead of other TX, resent if data keeps arriving); transmit side pauses the TX queue on XOFF from the host and resumes on XON; XON/XOFF bytes are taken out of the received stream rather than passed to the terminal.

Show the mode on the status line (as the RTS/CTS label is now), update README (Flow control section, SET-UP table) and tools/hostbridge.py (--rtscts, add --xonxoff). Host tests for the XON/XOFF logic (portable part split from serial.c), hardware check on the Pico 2.

title: Flash settings store usable at the 400 MHz DVI clock
description: SET-UP (dmt.6) must save settings to flash after video_init has raised clk_sys to 400 MHz. Nothing reads XIP after boot today (COPY_TO_RAM; only the copy loader and binary_info live at 0x10000000), but the SDK flash ops re-run the boot XIP setup, and the ROM routines pick their own SPI divisors, so the SCK rate at 400 MHz has to be checked per chip.
design: RP2350 (bootrom source, varm_generic_flash.c): flash_exit_xip -> flash_init_spi -> flash_enter_cmd_xip sets QMI direct mode and M0/M1 to 03h at CLKDIV 12 (BOOTROM_SPI_CLKDIV_DEFAULT), so ROM erase/program run at 33 MHz at 400 MHz: in spec, no change needed. Afterwards the SDK's flash_enable_xip_via_boot2 replays the boot RAM XIP stub (the mode and divisor the boot found at <=150 MHz, CLKDIV >=3, RXDELAY 2), which is 133 MHz+ at 400 MHz. That is only harmless while nothing reads XIP. Fix: xip_retime() = rom_flash_select_xip_read_mode(BOOTROM_XIP_MODE_03H_SERIAL, ceil(clk_sys/50 MHz)) after set_sys_clock_khz and after every erase/program, so settings can be read back and verified. RP2040 (bootrom program_flash_generic.c): flash_init_spi sets SSI BAUDR=6 (66.7 MHz at 400 MHz, no RX sample delay: same failure class as dmt.10), and it is only called from flash_exit_xip ('makes it possible for user code to edit SPI settings'). Fix: own RAM copy of the SDK erase/program sequence (connect_internal_flash, flash_exit_xip, then ssienr=0 / baudr=16 (25 MHz) / ssienr=1, ROM erase/program, flush_cache, re-enter XIP), then set XIP baudr to 8 as well. Both: call on core 0 without flash_safe_execute or multicore lockout (core 1 and all ISRs are in RAM, and a lockout would stall DVI). Leave IRQs on. A sector erase blocks core 0 for 30-400 ms; the serial RX ring absorbs that. Load settings at boot before video_init (the XIP config from boot is valid then). Store: last 2 flash sectors ping-pong, record = magic, version, seq, len, CRC32, data; newest valid wins, erase only the older sector.
acceptance_criteria: Save in SET-UP at 400 MHz on both targets without DVI dropout; settings survive power cycles; read-back verify passes; a UF2 reflash keeps the settings; power loss during a save leaves the previous settings.
notes: Implemented on branch setup-flash (src/nvflash.[ch], settings.[ch]); host tests + both firmware builds pass. Awaiting hardware check on both boards: save at 400 MHz without DVI dropout, survives power cycle, UF2 reflash keeps settings.
close_reason: Implemented (src/nvflash.[ch], settings.[ch]); verified on the Pico 2 (RP2350): settings save at 400 MHz and persist. RP2040 path built and host-tested only, see follow-up.

description: With the 720x480 raster pipeline, the default flash-resident build shows no DVI output, and the VIDEO_DIAG flash build prints nothing on UART0 TX, not even 'diag: boot' (the first thing main() does, at 125 MHz before the clock change). title: 80-column full-width option: Terminus 10x20 in 10-px cells filling 800x600
description:
Why: 80 columns uses 8-px cells and the 8x16 font, centred in 800x600 with 80 px black bars on both sides, and the 16-line glyph leaves 8 blank scanlines in each 24-line text row. A 10-px-wide font fills the screen with no video mode change: 80 x 10 = 800 px, clk_sys stays 400 MHz (same Z80 speed), and the monitor never resyncs. (Replaces the earlier idea of switching to 640x480 per column width. Pixel-stretching 8x16 to 10 wide was rejected: strokes come out 1 or 2 px depending on column.)

Font: Terminus 10x20 (Uni2-Terminus20x10.psf.gz from console-setup; same family, OFL licence and PSF loader as today's Uni2-Terminus16; 18x10 also exists). 20 glyph rows + 2 padding rows = 22 stored rows; glyph centred with 2 scanlines above and below.

Work:
- assets/fonts: add the PSF and note it in README/THIRD-PARTY.
- font_gen.py / cmake/fonts.cmake: emit 10-wide rows (two bytes per glyph row, or a packed form); the generated glyph ranges (DEC graphics, shades, blocks, box drawing 0x80-0x9F, control pictures) at 10 px; connectors must reach the cell edges.
- raster.h/raster.c: RASTER_MAX_FONT_ROWS 16 -> 20; raster_cell_width/x_offset/font_rows per layout; cell rows are 10 bits, so pack them: 22 rows x 100 bytes = 2200 bytes per line, in a union with the 132-col storage (max 15 rows x 132 = 1980). That is less than today's 18 x 132 = 2376, so raster memory shrinks ~4 KB (SRAM is the tight resource, ~28 KB free). Bold (shift within 10 px), underline, blink, reverse, cursor inversion.
- raster_compose (core 1, __not_in_flash_func, no const/flash data): a 10-px path, 5 pixel pairs per cell; similar per-scanline work to 132 cols' 400 pairs; check video_stats().late on hardware.
- settings: new append-only setting "80 columns: centred 8x16 (default, user preference) / full width 10x20"; applied like the column setting (re-render all lines). SET-UP label.
- Tests: test_raster variant for the 10x20 layout (stored-row mapping, packing, compose at cell boundaries, connectors); test_settings; check ESC sequences and DECCOLM switching 80<->132 with the option on.
- Docs: README, CLAUDE.md raster/font notes and resource budget.

Acceptance: host tests and firmware build pass; on hardware 80 columns fills the full width with the option on, 132 columns and the default centred layout unchanged, no late lines.

title: WORMS: detect the machine before touching clock ports (hangs on fz80, writes its disk port)
description: On the fz80 (fz80-firmware), WORMS hangs in CALIB: ports 65/66 are the fz80 disk controller's DSK_LOW/HIGH_ADDR (0x41/0x42); IN 0x42 is unhandled and returns 0, so CAL1 waits forever for the seconds to change (no BDOS calls, so no key gets out; reset needed). OUT (65) in CALIB and SEED also overwrites the low byte of the fz80's disk parameter block address. No CPR reply there either (cursor left bottom right; GETC timeout handles that).
design:
Pick a time source without blind OUTs:
1. BDOS 12: MP/M (01xxh) -> function 141 Delay (system ticks, fz80 50 Hz); CP/M 3 (31h) -> function 105 time to calibrate.
2. Else probe IN A,(50h) (read-only on both): 01h = fz80 (RTC_STATUS_PORT returns RTC_DONE_MASK) -> RTC millis counter (OUT (50h),2 then 4 reads of 51h), seed from PRNG port 70h; FFh = picosim/ours (unused port, IO_DATA_UNUSED) -> existing 65/66 clock, optionally confirm IN 65 in {0,1} and IN 66 BCD seconds; anything else -> no clock: fixed UNITMS, seed from R only, no OUTs.
3. Bound CAL1/CAL3 so a clock that never ticks cannot hang (fall back to fixed UNITMS).
Avoid: IN 64 (fz80 0x40 disk status read clears the result), other fz80 status reads that clear state; tick interrupts (too invasive for a .COM).
acceptance_criteria: WORMS runs on the fz80 without hanging and without writing disk ports; unchanged behaviour on the dvi-terminal CP/M machine; host tests pass.

title: Z80 core: undocumented X/Y flags (F bits 3/5) not modelled
description: CPUTEST (SuperSoft Diagnostics II) on Z80TESTS fails test 0025h: INC C (0C) leaves F=00H where a real Z80 gives 08H (bit 3 copied from the result). z80pack's Z80 cores (simz80*.c and ALT_Z80 altz80.h) never set X_FLAG/Y_FLAG: they model documented flags only, so EXZ80DOC passes but CPUTEST/ZEXALL do not. CP/M software rarely depends on these bits. Options: accept; patch z80pack (local patch or upstream PR); or swap in a core that models them (e.g. Superzazu z80, floooh chips) behind machine.c.
design: X/Y set in the vendored core via SET_XY/SET_XY_BLOCK (simdefs.h): result for ALU/INC/DEC/shifts/NEG/DAA/RLD/RRD/IN/LD A,I/R; CP's operand; BIT r: r, BIT (IX/IY+d): address high byte, BIT (HL): unchanged (no MEMPTR); SCF/CCF/CPL/RLCA..RRA: A; ADD HL/IX/IY,rr and ADC/SBC HL: high byte; LDI/LDD: byte+A, CPI/CPD: A-(HL)-H (bits 1/3). EXZ80ALL.COM (+ .MAC) added to Z80TESTS. Host: EXZ80DOC, EXZ80ALL all tests successful, CPUTEST 'CPU TESTS OK' (CPU_TESTS=1, ~3 min). Uncommitted; needs hardware check: CPUTEST and EXZ80ALL on the board (I reinstalls the disks).
notes: Reproduced by test_cpu (CPU_TESTS=1 scripts/test.sh, or build/test/test_cpu CPUTEST): CPUTEST still fails test 0025h (INC C, F=00H, should be 08H) after the DD/FD prefix fix; EXZ80DOC passes. CPUTEST stops at its first failure, so more X/Y differences may follow once this one is fixed. ALT_Z80 fails the same test (no X/Y either).
close_reason: CPUTEST and EXZ80ALL pass on hardware
